messages:
alex: Watching consistent queue growth on cache-sidecar in prod-3, latency spiking for prefix lookups. Started ~15:12 UTC. Any takers?

mira: i'm on it, pulling dashboards now. link: https://dash.redwood/prod3/cache

alex: top-level metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate=0.11 (10:45->11:15 window), in-flight queue=420, avg serve latency=180ms (was ~60ms). Backend QPS trending up.

cheng: seeing a lot of kernel fallback logs from runtime which is increasing CPU and slowing token pathing. might be related to big batch sizes hitting fallback kernels. snippet:
```
2026-03-18T15:12:34Z WARN kernel: fallback to generic_matmul for layer 12
2026-03-18T15:12:35Z INFO cache-sidecar: miss->backend queue len=134
2026-03-18T15:12:36Z DEBUG batching: batch_size=96 (heuristic override)
```

dmitri: looks like prefetch warmed many keys simultaneously for the same namespace -> backend thundering and evictions. prefix namespace "email-summaries" accounts for ~62% of recent misses.

alex: sample of recent counters: prefix_hit_rate: 0.09, backend_qps: 1200, evictions/sec: 78 -> sustained for ~20m.

mira: prefetch consumers show retry storms; backpressure not kicking in because per-namespace limiter is global currently. also see weird key normalization differences between SDK and router.

dmitri: suggestion: flip sidecar prefetch to read-through mode (synchronous) to avoid huge concurrent fanout. but that's slower for cold paths.

jen: product note: disabling prefetch will increase tail latency for first-time flows. need to communicate to support if we do emergency disable.

cheng: quick mitigation: decrease batching heuristic max_batch_size on prod-3 to 32 and throttle prefetch concurrency to 8 per namespace. that'll reduce kernel fallback pressure.

mira: @ops-bot can you suggest automated mitigation? preferring manual ops ok to be safe.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Recommended action: disable-sidecar-prefetch on cluster prod-3. Requires manual approval.

alex: i'm giving manual ok to disable. doing that now.

mira: disabling prefetch on prod-3 -> done. monitoring queue. initial drain starting.

sre-alerts: alert: cache-sidecar: queue_length decreased from 420 -> 70 in 3m after disable.

alex: after disable: backend qps reduced from 1200 -> 320, avg latency back to ~75ms. kv cache hit rate climbing gradually to 0.45 as caches warm from other traffic. kernel fallback logs also receding.

dmitri: confirmed: eviction/sec normalized, and we regained optimized kernels (no more fallback).

jen: please post an incident note to support and product channels describing user-visible impacts and mitigation steps.

cheng: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) implement per-namespace prefetch backpressure with jittered exponential backoff, 2) normalize prefix key hashing in SDK/router to avoid namespace fragmentation, 3) reduce max_batch_size adaptively when cache miss surge detected, 4) add kernel-fallback alert tied to cache-miss ratio, 5) add read-through toggle in runbook.

mira: adding owners: mira (runbook/monitoring), cheng (runtime heuristics), dmitri (cache policies), alex (incident lead), jen (customer comms).

alex: quick note: we observed subtle coupling between batching heuristic and cache miss storms — big batches amplify backend load when miss-rate > ~30%. we'll capture the profiling traces and include them in postmortem.

mira: attaching profiling snippet to postmortem draft (uploaded).

sre-alerts: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. reason: emergency disable of prefetch limited fanout.

alex: closing thread when postmortem + action items PR are up. thanks all.
